raw_response:
I have farmed this land a long time, so I will start from what worked for me before, not from empty talk. On 16.1 mu in Quzhou, with wheat-maize rotation and well water, I will keep the whole 16.1 mu in wheat for the winter season and the same 16.1 mu in maize after wheat harvest. I only finished primary school, but after 50 years I know where money should go. Fertilizer is expensive, but losing yield costs more, so I will not cut it too hard. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, because around here the better varieties usually stand better and yield more if water is available. For wheat, I will give the main fertilizer before sowing, then topdress nitrogen at jointing. I will water about 3 times if the year is normal: once before winter if soil is dry, once at jointing, once at grain filling. For maize, I will sow soon after wheat harvest, usually with less tillage to save time, and I will put more of the nitrogen as topdressing around the big bell stage. I watch what neighboring farmers do, and most people here do not dare underfeed wheat or maize. I also have some family working off-farm, so I will keep the plan practical and not too labor-heavy.
